limitations: Vectors derive from a private Fraction work-schedule oracle, not a public or target implementation.

The original .work/cp9-contract-oracle/report.json predating review1 materialized Fraction point objects before the canonicalize charge and retained dead face nodes. Review1 fixed those schedule-order and node-retention issues; review2 refreshed the decisions binding. Ignored oracle reports are optional provenance and are not required source bindings for these vectors.
The current private oracle still uses object-heavy exact arithmetic and is not memory or performance evidence.
The capacity ceiling is representational only. These small vectors do not exercise large allocation, native ownership/access, or target binary64 predicate implementation.
Reviewed vectors bind the canonical catalog hash; draft generation without a selected catalog has a null binding and cannot establish contract acceptance.

native_only_cases.description: NaN, +/-Infinity, and numeric carriers that cannot convert to finite binary64 are INVALID_INPUT before the canonicalize budget. Strict JSON intentionally carries no nonfinite literal.

Recognized wrong carriers (Java arbitrary Number subclasses, JavaScript typed-array/class point pairs, Python custom mapping/list containers) are INVALID_INPUT. Active getters/proxies/custom hooks are outside passive interchange and need not be read.
The duplicates-negative-zero success case supplies -0.0; output points and comparison bits must expose canonical +0. Native tests must cover ordinary numeric carriers and integral floating maxWork.

Ownership, detached materialization, accessor precedence, atomic destination writes, allocation failure, and the production packed-storage/no-dead-face requirement are native obligations, not claimed by these pure vectors.
